title: incident-bot: weighted sampling for on-call diagnostics quicklinks
author: Priya Rao
release_notes: Improves on-call quicklink relevance by introducing weighted sampling based on historical runbook success and SLO context. No customer-facing API changes.
description:
Motivation: on-call quicklinks surfaced by incident-bot were noisy when multiple runbooks matched; responders asked for higher-precision suggestions. This PR adds a lightweight weighted-sampling layer that biases quicklinks toward runbooks with higher historical helpfulness for similar SLO/context and recent on-call feedback. Design: - Maintain a per-runbook score computed from historical autodiagnostic hits, feedback votes, and recency decay. - At suggestion time, build candidate set then sample deterministically with weights (and a small epsilon chance to explore lower-ranked runbooks). - Expose tuning knobs via feature flags and runtime config (decay window, exploration epsilon). Implementation touches the runbook scorer, the candidate generation pipeline, and metrics emitted by the incident-bot service. Checklist:
- [x] Add runbook scoring pipeline and persistence layer (Redis hash + TTL for intermediate values)
- [x] Integrate weighted sampler into suggestion path
- [x] Add unit/integration tests and local harness script
- [x] Add opt-in feature flag and flag gating for rollout
- [x] Emit metrics (runbook_score distribution, suggestion_entropy, chosen_runbook_weight)
- [x] Update docs (oncall quicklinks behavior)
Rollout plan: feature flag off by default; enable for 10% of traffic for 48 hours, monitor suggestion_entropy, chosen_runbook_success_rate, and error rates. If metrics stable, ramp to 100% over 3 days. Linear tickets ENG-8043 (scoring infra) and ENG-8120 (runtime integration) track follow-ups. SUP-1234 filed for a customer request that motivated this change.
